text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. In a CI system, developers regularly add their code to a shared repository. This action automatically starts an automated build, which compiles the code and checks that everything works. The system then runs tests to make sure the new changes do not break existing features. By doing this often, teams can catch issues early, when they are easier and cheaper to fix. CI pipelines organise these steps into a clear process, from building to testing. As a result, software quality improves and releases become faster and more reliable.
